about: A sequel to a cave adventure. You are a returning hero with your old brass lantern, called to a final test by a silver-haired old man. You explore a dark underground realm with a stuck Elvish sword, a misty barren area and a shadowy hill land.

done.why: I left early after a short look. The Land of Shadow looked like a maze of repeating hills, and I had seen enough of the writing to rate it.

moments.note: Turning the lamp on revealed the junction and the sword in the rock.
The sword's hilt is worn to the shape of your hand.
Going west into the mist was blocked with a vivid in-world reason instead of a flat refusal.

wished: To read the runes on the sword.
To find out who the footsteps belong to.
To ask the lantern or the old man's dream more.

lines.line: It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come.
lines.why: Gives the lantern character and ties the world to earlier adventures.

lines.line: a hilt worn to the shape of a hand, which, when you close yours on it, turns out to be yours.
lines.why: A lovely, quiet hint that the sword is meant for you.

lines.line: the mist comes down over it thicker with every step, until you cannot see the ground you are walking on and have to turn back to find it.
lines.why: A refusal written as a small scene.

fun.why: Short and pleasant, but I barely got started.

engagement.why: The sword and the footsteps pulled at me, but the hill rooms looked repetitive.

difficulty.why: Nothing blocked me beyond the dark and the mist.

interestingness.why: A returning-hero frame, the sword and the follower hint make it intriguing.

prose.why: Careful, textured descriptions, especially the lantern, the sword and the mist refusal. The room text is more conventional.
